pins.name: D3
pins.label: GPIO0 (Button)
pins.notes:
Must be HIGH or floating for normal boot; LOW at boot enters flash/programming mode. No interrupt support. Onboard FLASH/BOOT pushbutton (active-low) — confirmed, see chipGpios note
Onboard FLASH/BOOT button (active-low) — see pfodWeb NOTE above pinNotes for sources

pins.name: D10
pins.label: D10 (GPIO1)
pins.notes: Hardware UART0 TX0 — used by the Serial pfod connection, not available as a general GPIO

pins.name: D4
pins.label: GPIO2 (Led active low)
pins.notes:
Must be HIGH at boot. Onboard LED on the ESP-12/ESP-12E module itself (active-low, D4/LED_BUILTIN) — confirmed, see chipGpios note
Onboard LED on the ESP-12/ESP-12E module (active-low, D4/LED_BUILTIN) — see pfodWeb NOTE above pinNotes for sources

pins.name: D9
pins.label: D9 (GPIO3)
pins.notes: Hardware UART0 RX0 — used by the Serial pfod connection, not available as a general GPIO

pins.name: D8
pins.label: D8 (GPIO15)
pins.notes: Must be LOW at boot (tied to GND via resistor on most boards)

pins.name: D0
pins.label: GPIO16 (Led active low)
pins.notes:
RTC-domain pin: no internal pull-up/down, no PWM, no interrupt support. Onboard LED on the NodeMCU devkit PCB (active-low, D0/LED_BUILTIN_AUX) — confirmed, see chipGpios note. Also commonly wired to RST for deep-sleep wake
Onboard LED on the NodeMCU devkit PCB (active-low, D0/LED_BUILTIN_AUX) — see pfodWeb NOTE above pinNotes for sources

pins.name: A0
pins.label: A0 (GPIO17)
pins.notes: Analog input only (A0) — cannot be used for digital I/O or PWM. NodeMCU has an on-board resistor divider giving A0 a 0-3.2V range (unlike the bare chip's native 0-1.0V) - see adc note below
